quickstart.lead: Community scores for games, movies, TV series and books — 0 to 100, in six categories per item — over a read-only JSON API.
quickstart.keyBody: Open your API dashboard and create a key. It starts with hx_live_ and is shown only once — store it in an environment variable, never in client-side code:
quickstart.freePlan: The Free plan includes {quota} requests in total — enough to build and test an integration.
quickstart.requestBody: The base URL is {baseUrl}. Every endpoint is a GET. Here are the five best-rated games:
quickstart.hostNote: The same API also answers on the website host: {siteUrl}. Paths, parameters and responses are identical.
quickstart.responseBody: Lists return data plus a next_cursor for the next page. Field names are snake_case and dates are ISO 8601. score and categories are null until an item has 5 ratings.
quickstart.nextDetail: Fetch one item with {path} for external ids, trailers and the licensed synopsis.
quickstart.nextLookup: Map ids you already have with {path} (also steam, igdb, tmdb, isbn13, openlibrary, wikidata).
quickstart.nextGuides: Handle <errors>errors</errors> and <limits>rate limits</limits>, then browse the <reference>API reference</reference>.
quickstart.sdkBody: Typed clients are generated from the OpenAPI document: TypeScript ({tsPackage}) and Python ({pyPackage}). They are not on npm/PyPI yet — build them from sdks/ in the repository until the first release.

authentication.lead: Every request is authenticated with a secret API key sent as a Bearer token.
authentication.bearerBody: Send the key in the Authorization header. Keys look like hx_live_ followed by 32 letters and digits. Query-string keys are not accepted, so keys never end up in access logs or browser history.
authentication.unauthorized: A missing, malformed, unknown or revoked key returns 401 with {problemCode} and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header.
authentication.manageCreate: Create and revoke keys at <link>/profile/api</link> (verified email required, up to 5 active keys).
authentication.manageOnce: The full key is shown once. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored; we cannot recover it for you.
authentication.manageRevoke: Revocation is immediate. Rotate by creating a new key, deploying it, then revoking the old one.
authentication.manageShared: All keys of an account share the same plan, quota and per-second rate limit.
authentication.securityNote: Call the API from your server. A key embedded in a web page or mobile app can be extracted and used up your quota. If a key leaks, revoke it right away.

errors.lead: Errors use RFC 9457 problem details with a stable machine-readable code.
errors.formatBody: Every error has Content-Type: application/problem+json. Branch on code (stable) rather than on title or detail (human text that may change). type links to the matching section below, and request_id equals the X-Request-Id header — include it when you contact support.

bad_request.title: Invalid request
bad_request.when: A query parameter is unknown or out of range, the cursor was tampered with or belongs to another query, or limit is above your plan's page size (10 on Free). errors lists each problem with its path.
bad_request.fix: Fix the listed parameters. Not counted against your quota when the parameters fail validation.

unauthorized.title: Missing or invalid API key
unauthorized.when: No Authorization: Bearer header, a malformed key, or a key that does not exist or was revoked.
unauthorized.fix: Check the header and the key at <link>/profile/api</link>. Never retried automatically.

payment_required.title: Quota exhausted
payment_required.when: The quota is exhausted: the 100 lifetime requests on Free, or the monthly quota plus prepaid credits on paid plans. The body includes plan and limit.
payment_required.fix: Upgrade or buy credits at <link>/pricing</link>. Paid quotas reset on the 1st of each month (UTC).

forbidden.title: Forbidden
forbidden.when: The account that owns the key is suspended.

not_found.title: Not found
not_found.when: Unknown item id, an id that belongs to another type (e.g. a game id under /movies), an unknown type path, or no match for /lookup.
not_found.fix: Check the id and the type. Lookups require an exact id (e.g. tt0111161).

rate_limited.title: Too many requests
rate_limited.when: More requests per second than your plan allows. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait. Not counted against your quota.
rate_limited.fix: Wait Retry-After seconds and retry; space out bursts or upgrade for a higher rate.

internal_error.title: Internal error
internal_error.when: Something failed on our side. The request is refunded to your quota.
internal_error.fix: Retry with exponential backoff. If it persists, send us the request_id.

service_unavailable.title: Service unavailable
service_unavailable.when: A dependency is temporarily down. Comes with Retry-After.

errors.retriesBody: Retry only 429, 500 and 503, honouring Retry-After when present and backing off exponentially otherwise. Every endpoint is a read-only GET, so retries are always safe.

pagination.lead: List endpoints use opaque cursors: stable under inserts, fast at any depth.
pagination.howBody: GET /games, /movies, /series and /books return {shape}. To get the next page, repeat the same request with {param}. When next_cursor is null you reached the end.
pagination.sameParams: Keep every other parameter identical. A cursor from another sort returns 400.
pagination.opaque: Cursors are opaque: do not parse or build them, their format may change.
pagination.stable: Ordering is stable: ties are broken by item id, and unscored or undated items always come last.
pagination.limitBody: limit defaults to 10. The maximum depends on your plan: {free} on Free, {paid} on Pro and Business. A larger value returns 400 bad_request — the API never silently truncates. Each page counts as one request.
pagination.searchBody: GET /search is not paginated: it returns the best matches (up to 50) for a query, best first.

limits.lead: Each plan has a request quota, a per-second rate limit and a maximum page size.
limits.pricing: Prices and upgrades: <link>/pricing</link>. Credits are prepaid requests spent only after the monthly quota runs out; they do not expire with the month.
limits.countEvery: Every authenticated request that reaches an endpoint counts as one, including 404s.
limits.countNot: Not counted: 401, 400 for invalid parameters, 429 and any 5xx (refunded).
limits.countUsage: GET /me/usage counts too — read the response headers of your regular calls when you can.
limits.countReset: Paid quotas reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month. The Free quota never resets.
limits.headersBody: Successful responses tell you where you stand (IETF RateLimit header fields):
limits.headerLimit: Requests in the current period (your plan quota).
limits.headerReset: Seconds until the quota resets; 0 for the lifetime Free quota.
limits.headerRetry: On 429 and 503: seconds to wait before retrying.
limits.exceedingNote: Too many requests per second → 429 rate_limited: wait Retry-After seconds. Quota (and credits) exhausted → 402 payment_required: upgrade or buy credits; retrying will not help until the reset.

changelog.lead: The version is part of the path. v1 only changes in backwards-compatible ways.
changelog.policyAdditive: Within /v1 we only make additive changes: new endpoints, new optional parameters, new response fields, new enum values in categories keys for new types, and new error detail texts. Ignore unknown fields and do not rely on field order.
changelog.policyBreaking: Breaking changes — removing or renaming a field, changing a type, making a parameter required — ship as a new path (/v2). Error code values, category keys and sort names are part of the contract.
changelog.deprecationWindow: A deprecated version keeps working for at least 6 months after its successor is released.
changelog.deprecationHeaders: Its responses carry Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers with the date it stops working, plus a Link to this page.
changelog.deprecationEmail: Account owners with recent traffic on the old version are emailed at deprecation and 30 days before sunset.
changelog.openapiI18nBody: /openapi.pt-BR.json and /openapi.es.json: the same contract as /openapi.json with descriptions in Portuguese and Spanish. Paths, field names and enum values are unchanged.
changelog.timeToBeatBody: ItemDetail.time_to_beat: crowdsourced median hours and report count for main, extras and completionist on games (median_hours is null under 3 reports); null for movies, series and books.
changelog.firstLists: Lists, details and genres for games, movies, series and books.

reference.lead: Every endpoint, parameter and response schema of the public API, generated from the OpenAPI document.
